_README: TRANCHE 14 v2 - LCW0 / LCW1 / LCW2. Re-keyed against your three schema corrections.
Four bodies. Last body-text tranche before the assembler.
WHAT CHANGED FROM v1, all yours:
a. clause_key is `landlord_work` throughout, not `landlord_contribution_work`. I invented
that key from the template's heading. `landlord_work` is the clause already registered
in loi_deferred_clause. My error, and exactly the kind the division of labour exists to
catch - I don't get to name schema.
b. The security position carries brace_code NULL, not 'LCW1'.
loi_position_variant_brace_uk is UNIQUE (variant_id, brace_code) WHERE brace_code IS NOT
NULL, so two positions in one variant both carrying LCW1 are rejected at load. It is an
UNCODED MODIFIER: brace null, emit_order set, applies_when gating on LCW1 selected AND
the $200k condition.
c. template_paragraph is INTEGER, not a symbolic name. 'lcw1_body' was invented. Both LCW1
positions carry 110, the template paragraph index. LCW0 (107) and LCW2 (112) are anchors
- groups of one - so they stay NULL rather than being given their own indices. A
non-null value there would create a group that a future position could join by accident.
Say if you would rather every body carry its index.
d. lcw2_building_incl is a TWO-option choose_one: the text plus an is_omit branch, keyed
like utilities_optional_1. Your correction stands - the tranche-11 params only looked
single-option because the dump swallowed their is_omit rows through NULL concatenation.
The '>= 2 options' guard was never violated and needs no amendment. I have marked the
omit branch with `is_omit: true`; if your seed shape expresses it differently, that flag
is the intent and the shape is yours.
CONTRACT G - keyed to match, no body change needed.
G deletes the token plus exactly one immediately-preceding space. Checked against all three
bodies here and they were already written for it:
LCW0/LCW1  '...improvements {{extras}} ('   -> '...improvements (the "Allowance")'
LCW2       '...Premises, {{incl}} including' -> '...Premises, including, without limitation'
Both single-spaced. Nothing to re-key.
THE ORPHAN ']' IS RESOLVED - and it is not what either of us feared.
You said only the Aug 2026 handbook could settle it. I have the handbook; you don't. Settled.
Both handbook editions render LCW2's header as:
'{LCW2} ALTERNATIVE - IF LANDLORD IS DELIVERING PREMISES IN CURRENT CONDITION AND NOT
PROVIDING WORK] [NOTE: NEVER INCLUDE THE TERM "AS-IS" IN ANY LOI - Landlord will not be
required to install ... any such defect.]'
The NOTE bracket opens and is never closed after 'LOI' - the body runs INSIDE it and the
trailing ']' closes the NOTE. The template closes the NOTE early instead ('...IN ANY LOI]')
and keeps the trailing ']' as well, which is why it looks orphaned there.
So the ']' belongs to the instruction, NOT to the Common Areas block. The block is
UNCONDITIONAL and stripping the bracket retains nothing that should have been optional. Your
residual risk is closed, not carried forward. The feasibility-study sentence sits outside the
bracket in both sources and is unconditional too.
ONE VARIANT NOTED, NOT ACTED ON: the Southeast doc reads 'other mechanical systems' where the
template and both handbooks read 'other mechanical and utility systems'. Template is body-text
authority, so 'and utility' is what is extracted here.
ASSEMBLER LOCATION - that one is already decided, and I don't think it should reopen.
The handoff records it as locked: a SEPARATE deterministic service, direct OVIS->service HTTP
job call with an idempotency key, not MCP, doing in-place surgery on the real template .docx.
The reasoning behind it still holds - OVIS decides and projects, the service renders, and the
renderer is deal-agnostic and database-free, which is what makes contract F coherent (OVIS
runs the exclusion check and the deferred halt; the assembler cannot re-check and doesn't).
Put it inside OVIS and the assembler gains database access, which is exactly the property F
depends on it not having.
If something you have found since makes that wrong, say what - I would rather reopen it on a
reason than have it drift. Otherwise treat it as settled and scope to it.

clauses.description: CLAUDE CODE ADDITION to tranche 14: position structure, which is not body text. Mike sent bodies only, by design.
clauses.guidance_note: LCW0/LCW1/LCW2 are a RANKED LADDER, not a selector: they partition on WHAT THE LANDLORD PROVIDES (work+allowance / allowance instead of work / neither), and unlike rent_basis these ARE preferences - LCW0 is the ask, LCW1 the documented FALLBACK, LCW2 the ALTERNATIVE. The template says so in its own markers. LCW1 is keyed despite the Aug 2026 handbook dropping it: body text comes from the template, and one source dropping it is not the retirement signal (see the decisions doc). template_paragraph is populated on EVERY position, not only the grouped pair, so contract B can anchor by index instead of falling back to fragile heading matching; accidental grouping is caught by the completeness test listing every multi-member paragraph group.
